label: YS-27
title: Post-cutover assert does not verify newMinter retains canMint: a wrong-constant operator error silently disables the replacement minter
description: The post-assert block (lines 126-138) confirms that OLD_MINTER.canMint is false and that OLD_MINTER is no longer an authorized client on YS_DOLA_OLD and YS_USDC_OLD. However there is no assertion that IFlaxMinter(PHUSD).authorizedMinters(newMinter).canMint remains true. The preflight at lines 86-88 confirms newMinter.canMint before revoking, but there is no re-verification after the three revocation calls. If an operator mistakenly supplies the newMinter address as the OLD_MINTER constant (transposing the two constants), the revocation at line 115 would disable the replacement minter. The post-asserts would still pass because they only check that the constant OLD_MINTER is revoked — the revoked address being newMinter would be invisible. The remaining mint path would be nobody.
impact: A constant transposition by the operator would atomically revoke both the old and new minters, leaving phUSD minting completely disabled with no mint path. Recovery requires a new setMinter(newMinter, true) owner transaction. No funds at risk but availability is disrupted.
recommendation: Add `require(IFlaxMinter(PHUSD).authorizedMinters(newMinter).canMint, 'Post-assert: newMinter lost mint authority during cutover')` to the post-assert block. This closes the footgun at zero cost and catches a constant transposition before the operator relies on the stale UI reminder in lines 141-144.
